C01_autogain+equalweight.title: Auto-gain (X05) + every position counts the same (X04)
C01_autogain+equalweight.hypothesis: X05 fixes the EMG size change between sessions and X04 makes the fit care about small positions; they address different causes, so together they may add up. Risk: interaction (both re-weight what the model sees at the weak positions).

D01_cleanpassive+autogain+equalweight.title: Best candidate: clean passive table (X01) + auto-gain (X05) + equal weight per position (X04)
D01_cleanpassive+autogain+equalweight.hypothesis: The Stage B best candidate C01 (meets criteria 1-3 on YES+EG, fails the noise criterion because of YES -0.49) plus the JM passive-table bug fix generalises to the 4 subjects not used for screening.

D02_D01+window_0.5s.title: Final candidate D01 with a 0.5 s input window (50 samples instead of 20)
D02_D01+window_0.5s.hypothesis: A teammate reported that a 500 ms window helped the original pipeline. A longer history might also help D01, although X06 (0.4 s on the baseline) was worse at Stage A.

S2_cleanpassive+autogain.title: Ladder step 2: clean passive table (X01) + auto-gain (X05), before equal weight
S2_cleanpassive+autogain.hypothesis: Not a new hypothesis: the intermediate step of the cumulative ladder last semester -> + clean passive -> + auto-gain -> + equal weight (= D01), so every step can be shown for every subject.

T01_passive_value_input.title: Passive-trial value of each trial as an extra input (Tier 2)
T01_passive_value_input.hypothesis: Under the passive-trial key, the relaxed (resting) level of the target at the toes-down positions shifts between sessions by up to 0.72 Nm (YES -0.49), because the passive-trial value changes between sessions while the relaxed torque inside the trial changes less (report 1: relaxed ~0.8 x passive). Giving the model the passive-trial value of the trial (measured before the trial, so available at prediction time) lets it learn how the resting target depends on that value across angles, and apply it to the new session.

X00f_baseline_framework.title: LSTM-8 baseline run through the experiment framework
X00f_baseline_framework.hypothesis: Reproduces X00 (frozen original code) exactly; used as the reference for every experiment and for the S2→S1 direction.

X01_clean_passive.title: Clean passive table (static holds only)
X01_clean_passive.hypothesis: The original passive table accepted pieces of passive trials that were not relaxed (JM: +11.7 Nm entry). Using only the still, steady holds removes that labelling error; it should fix JM at −0.08 rad and change nothing elsewhere.

X02a_dropout_0.0.title: Dropout 0.0 (baseline 0.3)
X02a_dropout_0.0.hypothesis: If the baseline is over-regularised (underfits), less dropout improves the weak positions.

X02c_dropout_0.5.title: Dropout 0.5 (baseline 0.3)
X02c_dropout_0.5.hypothesis: If the baseline overfits session 1, more dropout improves generalisation to session 2.

X03_lr_0.001.title: Learning rate 0.001 (baseline 0.003)
X03_lr_0.001.hypothesis: If training is unstable (large run-to-run differences), a smaller learning rate gives more stable and better solutions.

X04_equal_angle_weight.title: Every position counts the same in the fit (divide each position by its typical swing)
X04_equal_angle_weight.hypothesis: Plain least squares in Nm² lets the strong positions dominate (YES: 2 most plantarflexed positions = 1 % of the loss). Dividing each position's target by its training standard deviation (= weighted least squares, weight 1/σ²) should improve the plantarflexed positions without hurting the others much.

X05_autogain.title: EMG auto-gain (running per-muscle rescaling, off for people who push both ways)
X05_autogain.hypothesis: The EMG size for the same push changes between sessions (JM ≈ 0.4–0.5× at some positions). Rescaling each muscle by its own recent quiet and strong levels should make session 2 look like session 1.

X06_window_0.4s.title: 0.4 s input window (baseline 0.2 s)
X06_window_0.4s.hypothesis: A longer history gives the model more context for small, slow pushes.
